import os,resource; os.sched_setaffinity(0,sorted(os.sched_getaffinity(0))[:2]); resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU,(115,115)); resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS,(6*1024**3,6*1024**3)); from pathlib import Path import subprocess,sys s='''# Independent ordinary proof: MathDB 368088 Reconstructed from raw/literal and the mechanism disclosed in TASK, before opening FULLCANDIDATE.md. Independent verification, not independent invention. Let P* be the primes greater than 3. A prime in P* is divisible by neither 2 nor 3: otherwise its positive divisor 2 or 3 would equal it. Division with remainder by 6 therefore gives residue 1 or 5. Define f(p)=p for residue 1 and f(p)=p-1 for residue 5, and Q=f(P*), a set (not a multiset) of positive natural numbers. The images of the two branches have residues 1 and 4 modulo 6 respectively. Equality across branches is impossible; within a branch equality cancels the same shift and implies equality of primes. Thus f is injective. Its outputs are positive (p>=5 implies p-1>=4) and all have residue 1 modulo 3. In particular Q has no elements at most 3. Define both counting functions on integer cutoffs using finite sets of natural numbers embedded in the integers. For n>=3 let A={p prime:3 {q in Q:q<=n}. For forward inclusion: p in A has f(p)<=p<=n; for p in E, f(p)=p-1=n. For surjectivity take the unique preimage p of q<=n. If p<=n then p belongs to A. Otherwise p>n; the fixed branch would give q=p>n, impossible. On the other branch p-1<=n

1 would have a prime divisor, obtained by choosing its least divisor >1, and this divisor divides none of the listed primes' product, a contradiction. Removing 2,3 leaves infinitely many; injectivity of f makes Q infinite. Neither arithmetic-progression infinitude nor a prime-pattern theorem is needed. For every natural threshold N choose n=3(N+1). The integer 2n=6(N+1) is even and exceeds N, since 6(N+1)-N=5N+6>0. Every sum of two Q elements has residue 2 modulo 3, whereas this 2n has residue 0. Therefore no q1,q2 in Q sum to it. This applies also when q1=q2, and remains a refutation if distinct summands were required. It proves the full negation: there exists one qualifying Q such that for every natural N there is an even integer 2n>N without a Q representation. No experiment, enumeration, PNT, classical Goldbach assumption, or formal checker was used. The finite-set bijection, not mere bounded movement, is what pays the uniform counting assertion. Including or excluding zero in the convention for naturals does not affect this positive witness. Source visual fidelity is to be checked separately. ''' r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','-B',str(Path.cwd()/'write_lane.py'),'PROOF.md'],input=s,text=True,capture_output=True,timeout=10);print(r.stdout);assert r.returncode==0,r.stderr
